question: Do frozen Ca_HVA gate primitives retain accuracy on voltage paths actually visited by the full 642-segment teacher?

source.dataset: canonical targeted diagnostic v1.1 base, 29,240 transitions

design.microtrace_grid: 41 voltage samples at 0.025 ms from 0 to 1 ms
design.fine_update: 40 right-boundary samples V[1:41] at dt=0.025 ms, following Task 7c boundary semantics
design.coarse_update: 8 right-boundary samples V[5],V[10],...,V[40] at dt=0.125 ms

evaluation.primary: candidate gate and m^2h errors versus exact formula composed on recorded fine path
evaluation.teacher_floor: exact-formula fine-path endpoint versus stored authentic teacher m,h endpoint
evaluation.teacher_floor_rule: If max(m RMSE,h RMSE)>0.005 in any nonempty site/regime group, report candidate-vs-teacher values as non-interpretable; candidate-vs-formula remains a numerical approximation diagnostic.
evaluation.support_rule: Any unfilled site/regime quota is reported as a support shortfall; no replacement, retrospective threshold change or extrapolated claim.
evaluation.secondary: candidate endpoint versus teacher, conditioned on calibrated teacher floor

limitations: The path is recorded from the future full-teacher trajectory and is legitimate only for this teacher-forced diagnostic. It cannot be passed to an autonomous closed-loop predictor. The source microtrace is float32 and CVode integrates between samples, so formula-vs-teacher disagreement is a measured reference floor rather than silently attributed to candidates.
